Following up with the technical appendix and inline answers to the numbered items in your questionnaire. I've attached a printable appendix PDF and pasted the highlights below for quick review.

(Attachment: technical-appendix-aurora.pdf)

--- Inline Q&A (high level, see appendix for diagrams & timings) ---
Q1 — RTO / RPO commitments (hosted API):
- Standard hosted offering: RTO target for region-to-region automated failover is 5 minutes for control-plane and routing changes; application-level warm paths typically restore within 60–180 seconds depending on model size and prefix cache hit-rates.
- RPO: for request-response state we are stateless; model artifacts and persistent storage replicate asynchronously across paired regions with a configurable RPO window. Default RPO is 15 minutes for model artifacts and 24 hours for snapshot backups of customer-managed metadata.
- Dedicated / Private deployments: RTO/RPO depend on customer topology and WAN links; typical benchmarked RTO for private VPC-based switchover we document is 10–20 minutes with pre-warmed standby capacity. We provide runbook steps to achieve sub-10-minute cutovers when customers maintain hot-standby nodes.

Q2 — Failover orchestration and cold-start latency:
- Orchestration: our control plane triggers a three-stage switchover: (1) route reallocation and DNS/edge updates, (2) capacity allocation and model boot + KV cache reconstruction, (3) traffic ramp with canary and progressive routing.
- Cold-starts: measured cold-start to first-token for larger models (40B+) on typical GPU hardware is ~20–45s to boot weights + 5–30s to warm KV/prefix cache depending on workload. For optimized quantized variants (8-bit) median first-use latency is 8–15s.
- Mitigations: prefix/KV caching, on-demand warm pools, and model-variant fallbacks reduce perceived outage; we also support cross-region request draining to preserve in-flight requests during switchover.

Q3 — Backup retention and restore testing:
- Backups: control plane and customer metadata snapshots retained per customer policy; default retention 30 days, options up to 7 years for enterprise.
- Restore: automated restore playbooks tested quarterly; we publish summarized test reports upon request and can provide a redacted restore runbook and a recent test window log for audit.

Q4 — Audit logs & export cadence:
- Audit logs capture control-plane actions, admin API calls, and per-request routing traces with millisecond timestamps.
- Export: logs are available via S3 export (or customer SIEM integration) with daily and on-demand snapshot exports. Retention/formatting configurable; we can provide a 30-day sample export for procurement review.

Notes & caveats:
- SLA language: we provide availability SLAs by deployment type; RTO/RPO are operational commitments and, where required, can be codified in a continuity addendum or included in Dedicated contracts.
- Private/on-prem: items around data egress and physical replication are customer-specific — we’ll include a checklist for network prep if you plan an air-gapped/private rollout.

I’ll be on the walkthrough next Thursday; Ben, please confirm the time.
